review.tagline: Terminal coding agent that fans work out across many models
review.summary: OmO is an `omo` command-line agent, built on senpi (a fork of pi), that reads a codebase, plans, and verifies each step. Typing `ulw` or `mass ulw` turns a job into a graph of parallel agents, each on a different model. Memory is kept as markdown files in a git repository, and `/login` covers Claude, ChatGPT, Kimi and GLM subscriptions.
review.audience: Developers wanting a terminal coding agent mixing several model subscriptions
strengths: Splits jobs across many agents and models in parallel with the `mass ulw` keyword
Memory stored as markdown in a git repo, so it is inspectable and versionable
Native binary installer with checksum verification, plus bun and npm packages
`omo setup` imports keys, MCP servers and skills from the OpenCode edition
weaknesses: License is SUL-1.0, not a standard OSI license; check terms before commercial use
Primary install path pipes a curl script into bash
README gives no RAM, token cost or hardware figures
needs: Needs Model provider subscription or API keys, git (memory repository)
